correctness.rationale: For every order \(n\ge2\), each \((n-1)\)-state \(v\) induces a binary permutation of incoming labels. A length-\(n+1\) palindrome is precisely a fixed point of that permutation at a palindromic v. Binary permutations have 0 or 2 fixed points, and constant states must be swaps or a self-loop would separate from the Euler tour. Thus the universal parity/bound proof is deductive. The order-five full \(2^{16}\) assignments were enumerated and classified by the single-32-cycle test (65536/2048); independent direct Euler tour backtracking reconstructed the same 768/512/512/256 profile. Both methods and exact source code are packaged. No finite data are used as proof of higher-order counts.

value.rationale: Length \(n+1\) is the first cyclic factor length no longer prescribed by the de Bruijn property. The all-order even-pairing law is a structural constraint on this natural boundary, and the complete order-five joint occurrence table resolves two coupled nonconstant palindromic overlap states. Its negative joint dependence and attainable \(0,2,4\) spectrum cannot be read off from the mean or the longest-palindrome table; it is a motivated finite classification with an infinite-order companion theorem, not an arbitrary slice or a mere known-table recomputation.
